scope.applicability: Human decision placement within one exact workflow instance.
exclusions: The Authority Boundary governing a decision.
Automated validation or generated projection refreshes.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Decision Checkpoint is one workflow-local position at which a closed set of required Governance Decisions may be presented as one human interaction. It carries no authority by itself. Its placement is resolved from a Workflow Decision Profile and an applicable User Decision Preference, while every decision presented there retains its own Authority Boundary, accountable owner, exact target, and effect.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: DecisionCheckpoint(w,c) iff c in Allowed(Profile(Type(w))) and Resolved(Profile(Type(w)),Preference(User(w),Type(w))) = c. Authority(c) = none.
boundary_conditions: Approval is one possible decision outcome, not the checkpoint itself.
Grouping decisions at one checkpoint does not merge their Authority Boundaries.
A checkpoint cannot bind unknown future bytes when the required decision targets exact output bytes.
testable_conditions: An approval-requiring workflow resolves exactly one checkpoint.
The resolved checkpoint belongs to the workflow type's allowed set.
The checkpoint record has authority_effect none.

plain_language.explanation: The one place in a workflow where the person is asked to decide. Calling it a checkpoint avoids confusing where the question appears with what the person is allowed to authorize.

domain_context.explanation: CyberAlchemy Lab workflows should interrupt the user at no more than one configured checkpoint. That interaction can present several exact role-scoped decisions without collapsing them.
examples: A definition pack can be authored and validated before one admission checkpoint.
A representation migration can present both context-owner selections together only when the same principal holds both roles and both postimages exist.

boundaries: Decision Checkpoint is not Authority Boundary.
Decision Checkpoint is not Governance Decision or approval outcome.
Workflow position does not imply greater truth, evidence quality, or authority.
claim_ceiling: This candidate names workflow interaction placement only. It does not request, record, approve, reject, or authorize any decision or effect.
